newsitem.title: UK: Everard to dispose of two 1970s built tankers.
newsitem.headline: Everard to dispose of two 1970s built tankers.

text.p: British shipowner F.T. Everard is to dispose of two of its 1970s-built tankers as it takes delivery of two new clean petroleum products carriers built in Singapore.
Everard has recently taken delivery of the 3,778dwt Asperity from Keppel Singmarine Dockyard and her sistership, the Audacity, is currently on passage from Singapore.

Managing director William Everard told Reuters at a naming ceremony for the Asperity that the two new ships would replace the 3,419dwt Apricity and 3,402dwt Assurity. Both the former Esso-owned vessels were built in 1971.
He said: "The first ship is currently going up for sale and the other will follow when Audacity is delivered."
Everard said the older ships were being replaced because they did not fit in operationally with the new vessels which only need seven crew.
"With deballasting it takes 18 hours to load the old ships compared with a four and a half unloading capability for the new ships."
He added that the Audacity would enter service around the beginning of May.

Everard said the new ships would be 90 percent operated under contracts of affreightment with various oil majors, but be operated on the spot market when possible. It is likely that one ship will be largely employed on UK east coast and European trades while the other is employed on the west coast and to Ireland, he said.
The Asperity has already concluded five voyages including one spot charter.
Everard added: "These 4,250 cubic metre vessels are so far ahead of any others, that we hope they will give us an edge over the competition." - Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
